newsitem.title: USA: SEC moves toward greater electronic disclosures.
newsitem.headline: SEC moves toward greater electronic disclosures.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission is proposing that all investment managers who trade large volumes of securities disclose their holdings more efficiently on the agency's electronic filing system.

In its proposal announced last week, major investors such as Warren Buffett will have to make the quarterly reports, known as Form 13F, via the SEC's Electronic Data Gathering Analysis and Retrieval System rather than on paper.
The agency's latest proposal would be a landmark move further toward total electronic disclosure, leaving only a few filings submitted to the agency on paper.

"The public interest in having these reports, along with other filings, available electronically has increased, and the Commission believes these reports should have the same degree of availablility as other Commission filings," it said.
SEC requires institutional investment managers holders of at least $100 million certain companies to make the quarterly filings.
